Amina Nzue, stall clerk on the dawn shift, copied four sack quotes onto the thin carbon before the lorry left the yard at [[place]]Mitzic[[/]]. She dated that sheet [[filed]]3 March 2026[[/]] and kept the rows in the order the sellers called them. Cassava came in at [[comp]]110[[/]], plantain at [[comp]]140[[/]], smoked fish at [[comp]]180[[/]], and the palm-oil tins at [[comp]]220[[/]]. Buyers were already arguing over plantain at the gate, and the driver kept the engine idling. A drawer scrap from the prior season still showed 95, and she left that scrap unmarked. In the margin she wrote vu et transmis. The rubber stamp smeared, so recei
ved broke onto the next line. She did not print a centre figure on this page.

ask.instruction: What count sits between the two central quotes?

marked_text:
Pascal Obame, pump fitter, came off the night shift and walked the shed at [[place]]Booue[[/]] with a stub of pencil. The generator coughed once and the shed bulb flickered, but he finished the round before it died. He logged the taps in the order of that walk. Tap A stood at [[comp]]8[[/]], tap B at [[comp]]12[[/]], tap C at [[comp]]15[[/]], tap D at [[comp]]19[[/]], tap E at [[comp]]24[[/]], and the yard tap at [[comp]]30[[/]]. A cracked card from 2024 still showed 33, and he left it unmarked because the glass was fogged. He muttered bon pour classement. The carbon caught on the fold and pressu
re tore into two pieces. He trusts only the six taps from this morning.

ask.name: fair_reading
ask.instruction: What reading sits between the two central taps?

marked_text:
Sylvie Mba, timber scaler, set eight lot weights on the damp yard sheet at [[place]]Ndjole[[/]] and dated the ticket [[scaled]]14 June 2027[[/]]. The crew had stacked the lots under a torn tarp, and she checked each tag before she wrote the figure. She kept the walk order: [[comp]]400[[/]], then [[comp]]500[[/]], then [[comp]]700[[/]], then [[comp]]900[[/]], then [[comp]]1100[[/]], then [[comp]]1300[[/]], then [[comp]]1500[[/]], and last [[comp]]1700[[/]] kilograms. A rejected bundle pencilled at 850 never reached the scale. Under the column she wrote vu pour cubage. Rain hit the stamp and kilo
grams broke onto the next line. She left the centre of the column blank.

A peg from a prior week still read 36, and he kept that scrap out of the run. In the corner he wrote vu au matin. Damp paper made morn
ing fall across the margin. The lines he stands by are these.

[[obs]]2026-05-02|44[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-05-03|48[[/]]
[[obs]]2026-05-04|53[[/]]
